product.name: agenticspec
product.lede: agenticspec reads the transcripts of your Claude Code sessions and turns them into numbers you can compare: cost, cache use, time spent waiting on you, refused tool calls, secrets that reached the agent. It runs on your machine and sends nothing anywhere.
product.description: Numbers about your coding-agent sessions, computed on your machine: cost, cache use, waiting time, refused calls, secrets. With a dashboard, a query language and pattern mining.
product.meta: Claude Code transcripts · runs locally · Apache-2.0

sections.title: From a transcript to a number.
sections.lede: Everything below runs on your machine. The store holds no prompt text and no tool output.

steps.label: read
steps.title: Read the transcripts
steps.description: Each record becomes a typed step: a prompt, a tool call, a permission decision, a model turn, with who acted.

steps.label: redact
steps.title: Replace secrets
steps.description: Secrets and personal data become aliases such as gitlab_token#1. Only the kind and the count are kept.

steps.label: store
steps.title: One SQLite file
steps.description: agenticspec sync adds new and changed sessions to a local store. Later runs take seconds.

steps.label: measure
steps.title: KPIs, queries, patterns
steps.description: The dashboard, the KPI report, queries and pattern mining all read the store.

sections.title: Four ways to look at your sessions.
sections.lede: Each item links to its page.

items.title: Dashboard
items.description: agenticspec serve: averages over a time window, the recent sessions with search, and each session in detail, updated live.

items.title: KPIs
items.description: Cost at API list price, cache hits and busts, concurrency, time working and time waiting on you, permission decisions.

items.title: Queries
items.description: Find sessions where something happened: a refused call asked for again, a long wait, a sub-agent result nobody read.

items.title: Patterns
items.description: Find runs of tool calls that repeat across sessions and export them as draft procedures.
